meta.title: npuforge - Sophos XGS hardware, back as OPNsense firewalls
meta.description: Free, open-source FreeBSD drivers and an OPNsense plugin that bring Sophos XGS 136 and XGS 3300 appliances back as open firewalls, the coprocessor forwarding connections and IPsec in hardware.

hero.title: Sophos XGS hardware, back as open firewalls
hero.lede: FreeBSD drivers, written against registers no vendor documents, and an OPNsense plugin around them. They hand the front ports back, then hand the coprocessor the firewall's own connections and IPsec associations, so its fast path forwards them without the host.
hero.photo_alt: Three Sophos XGS appliances on the bench: an XGS 136 on top and two XGS 3300s below, cabled port to port
hero.photo_caption: The bench: an XGS 136 and two XGS 3300s, each running OPNsense with every front port.
hero.drawing_caption: The two appliances run here, drawn as they stand on the bench: an XGS 136 on an XGS 3300. Point at a port for its interface; a click opens it on its model's page.

notice.title: New discoveries, 2026-10-22.
notice.text: A sweep of the vendor's sources and the coprocessor's own log found capabilities of this hardware that were not known - among them a deep packet inspection engine on the XGS 3300's coprocessor and the TCP window checked in hardware. The completion figures now count them, so they went down: the XGS 3300 to 89%, the XGS 136 to 91%. They will be worked on gradually and arrive as updates.
notice.link_text: The discoveries, with a drawing of where each one lives

problem.title: Two computers in one box
paragraphs: Install OPNsense on a Sophos XGS and it boots to a working firewall with no network interfaces at all. The appliance looks like one computer and is two: an x86 host, and a coprocessor behind a PCIe endpoint that owns every front port.

The vendor ships drivers for its own operating system and for Linux only, so when support lapses the usual verdict on the hardware is e-waste. This project gives the ports back to FreeBSD, and then puts the coprocessor to work for the firewall.

items.title: Every front port
items.text: All fourteen on the XGS 136 and all twelve on the XGS 3300, with its expansion module's, each an ordinary FreeBSD interface named as the chassis names it.

items.title: pf decides, the coprocessor forwards
items.text: A connection the firewall has passed goes into the coprocessor's flow table, IPv4 with its translation and IPv6 as it is, and comes back out the moment pf lets go of it.

items.title: IPsec in the engine
items.text: An association strongSwan installs through OPNsense lands on the coprocessor's crypto engine with nothing typed: AES-GCM, AES-CBC with an HMAC, NAT traversal.

items.title: The firewall's lists still cut
items.text: A block list gaining an address, or the Intrusion Detection logging a listed TLS fingerprint (JA4), cuts a connection that is already in hardware.

items.title: Part of OPNsense
items.text: One section of the menu, every page in Arabic and English, the front ports assigned at the first boot, and updates from its own page in seconds.

pages.title: It looks like OPNsense, because it is
pages.text: The XGS section of the menu shows the front panel with each port's link, the coprocessor, the flows in hardware, the IPsec engine, the transceivers, updates and problem reports. Every page is photographed on an appliance, in English and in Arabic.

story.title: The story
story.lede: How a firewall with no ports became one with every port: eight months of looking, the open sources read for what they say, two coprocessors that share nothing, and the last hop - told in eleven chapters, with the photographs.

modules.title: Expansion modules
modules.index_description: Every expansion module the vendor's board files describe for the XGS coprocessor's bay: its ports drawn, the PHYs behind them, and the appliances that take it.
modules.lede: The 1U appliances and the larger ones have a module bay in front, and it is the coprocessor's, not the host's: a module's ports are the coprocessor's own, and the drivers name each as it is on the metal - A1, A2 and on. Every module the vendor's board files describe is here, with the appliances whose datasheet lists it. One has been fitted and run here; the others fit models the drivers know and are added, untested, or fit only the larger families, which have no driver yet.
